- **Why `finding`, not queue**: real mechanism, but dormant today — the body's own consumer measurement (from #7378) shows no in-tree caller constructs a `MetadataFacade`. Nothing a user hits until one is wired; the findings-triage round grades promotion, and the body's note to ride the #7378 envelope ruling (rather than invent a second envelope) is a promotion-time constraint.
- **Dedup**: filer's zero-hit dup search accepted; independently checked the open list — the closest kin are #7378 (round-trip cells, `pm:dispatched`, distinct rows) and #7221 (unregisterPackage, different mechanism). No convergence needed.
- **`target:v17`**: no — dormant surface, not release-blocking.

Serial constraints cleared: `metadata-facade.ts` — **no open PR touches it** (lane in flight 0, enqueued 0 at claim time). ⚠️ **Same-day churn, ~30 minutes old**: **#8349** (#7378's implementation half) landed on this exact file. The dev branches from current `origin/main` and reads the merged text.

## The stated dependency is satisfied — verified, not assumed

This card was held because its fix depended on #7378's **cell 3**: *"if non-object `data` throws, the `{ name, content }` boxing it must unwrap disappears."* **It does.** #8349 removed both the boxing and the silent reconcile, and the facade's new docblock names this card's seam directly.

⚠️ **A grep alone said otherwise, and would have misled me**: searching `origin/main` for the boxing returns **1 hit** — which on reading is the docblock *describing the removal in past tense*. Same shape as a false alarm this seat hit earlier today on `via populate`. **A grep cannot distinguish a claim from a description of a claim**; the count is not the finding.

## Premise re-checked at claim time

The unwrap is **still present**, at addresses that have **moved**: `:202`, `:217`, `:259` (the card records `:149`, `:164`, `:204` from 08-11). ⛔ Locate by symbol — this file has churned three times since the card was filed.

## Model rationale

**`claude-fable-5`.** This determines what `MetadataFacade.get` / `list` / `listNames` **return** for every metadata type carrying a real `content` field (`doc`, `knowledge_document`), on the very `register` → `get` roundtrip contract the maintainer ruled two days ago. ⛔ The clause has no downward discretion and the card's small diff is not the criterion; when the surface is the one that was just ruled, the tier follows the surface.

## ⛔ Not escalated, and the threshold is worth stating

The fix picks an envelope mechanism, which *looks* like a design call. It is not one: the **invariant is already ruled**. #7378 row 1 settled that `register(t, n, d)` → `get(t, n)` either round-trips or **refuses loudly** — a shipped implementation silently returning something other than what was registered is the defect that ruling names. This is a restore-the-invariant fix (its own decision), so it goes to the queue rather than the decision box. ⛔ If the dev finds the invariant genuinely cannot be restored without a contract choice, that is a **reported fork**, not a silent pick.

## PM review — **ACCEPT on the merits**. PR #8377; landing held on CI convergence.

`domain:engine-core` seat (#6019), session `session_01RDTnVvsgA6cUZ4xFVtPZRy`. Reviewed against GitHub and the tree, ⛔ not the report's narrative.

**Path face** (read from the tree): exactly **4** files — the changeset, `metadata-facade.ts`, its test, and the objectql conformance driver. **0** hits under `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/skills/**`, `skills/**`, or `packages/spec/src/**`. ⭐ The fence held where it mattered: the new all-four-implementations pin went into the **driver-local** block, ⛔ not the shared table under `packages/spec/src/` — that table is the spec seat's half of #7378 and is tracked on **#8350**, which this card did **not** widen.

### ⭐ The dev answered a better question than I asked

I told it to pick an envelope mechanism and to *check which authorable key it might collide with next*. It did not pick one — it **measured that the envelope has no producer at all**:

- the only writer that ever produced one was the facade's own #7511 cell-3 boxing, which **#8349 replaced** with the shared guard's loud refusal;
- DB hydration (`loadMetaFromDb`) registers the **parsed document** from `sys_metadata.metadata`, never a wrapper;
- every other in-tree `registerItem` caller stores the document as-is.

With no envelope on any write path, an unwrap on the read path **can only corrupt**. So the fix is **removal, not a rename** — and there is no next authorable key to collide with, because **the collision surface is gone rather than moved**. That is strictly better than the safer-key answer my dispatch invited, and it is the reason this needed no envelope ruling.

It also removed the dead `listNames` `content?.name` limb **with the measurement of why it was dead in both directions**, rather than quietly.

### Verification credited

Reverse verification with the direction **and the specific set** predicted before running: unwrap restored ⇒ predicted red on `get`-document / `list` / `knowledge_document` / conformance-facade-subject, green on `listNames` / `exists` / `getEntry` / content-less. Measured **4 failed | 98 passed**, exactly that set, restored **from the committed branch** rather than working-tree memory. Full suite 196 files / 3506 tests green.

Blast radius **re-measured at HEAD** as I asked, not inherited from the card: `new MetadataFacade` appears only in tests and one migration doc, so the defect stays dormant until a host wires one — and the class is exported from the package root, so downstream hosts pick the fix up via the changeset.

### Docs advisory — checked, and clean

15 pages, all package-level `via @objectstack/objectql`. The one page mentioning `MetadataFacade` (`migration-from-objectql.mdx`) documents **construction and async-ness**, not the unwrap; its example registers an `object` with no `content` field, so the fix makes the round-trip it teaches *more* reliably true. **An honest negative** — the method that found real defects on three cards today found nothing here, and that is a result rather than a reason to keep digging.

### The out-of-scope finding is the more important half

**#8378**: the same `?.content ?? i` unwrap family survives in **production plugin read paths** — `plugin-security` ×3, `plugin-sharing`, `plugin-webhooks` ×2, `plugin-email` ×3 — over the same registry stores. ⚠️ Unlike the facade, those are **not dormant**. And the dev graded the nuance instead of smoothing it: `email-template` accepts `content` as an authorable **alias** spelling, and **whether a pre-conversion item can reach that read was not measured** — stated as unmeasured, not assumed safe. Filed unassigned with a `finding` label, ⛔ not self-promoted into this lane's queue; triage grades it, and its routing is likely `domain:identity` / `domain:services`, ⛔ not here.

Landing follows once every gate job carries its own conclusion.

## LANDED — PR #8377 merged 2026-08-13 11:48Z. Closed by the merge; `pm:dispatched` cleared.

`domain:engine-core` seat (#6019), session `session_01RDTnVvsgA6cUZ4xFVtPZRy`.

### What landed

All three reads return the stored document verbatim. The unwrap presumed `content` marked the facade's own storage envelope; `content` is a **real authorable field** (`doc.zod.ts` declares it as the doc's required raw-Markdown body, `knowledge-document.zod.ts` on both shapes), so `register('doc', n, d)` → `get('doc', n)` answered the Markdown string — truthy, string-typed, silent.

**Removal rather than a renamed envelope, measured not assumed**: the envelope has no producer. The facade's own interim boxing (#7511 cell 3) was replaced by the shared guard's loud refusal in #8349; DB hydration registers the parsed document itself; every other in-tree `registerItem` caller stores the document as-is. ⭐ Because no replacement key is introduced, **the collision surface is gone, not moved** — there is no next authorable key to collide with.

Both directions pinned, and the `listNames` `content.name` fallback limb was measured dead in both directions before removal. Reverse verification predicted the direction **before** running: 4 red / 98 green, exactly as predicted, with the fix restored from the committed branch rather than working-tree memory.

⚠️ The new conformance pin went in the driver-local *"beyond the table"* block, deliberately **not** the shared table — that lives under `packages/spec/src/` and is the spec seat's half of #7378, tracked on #8350. Fence respected.

### On the merge-queue ejection — recorded because the lane will hit this again

This PR was **dequeued at 10:55:27Z with `CI_FAILURE` and it was not this PR's failure.** Measured at the time: of the 12 jobs in #8377's own queue run, **five were `success` and seven were still `in_progress` — not one had failed.** It was first in a batch with #8383 stacked on it, and #8383 was re-formed onto the base 2 seconds after #8377 was dropped.

Re-queued standalone at 11:28Z on the **same commit, zero changes** → merged 20 minutes later. ⭐ **A merge-queue red is a batch verdict, not a PR verdict** — the discriminator is mechanism ("can this diff physically reach that code path?"), and this diff touches only a class with **no production caller**. Same shape as #8216. ⛔ Re-queueing before reading the run's own jobs would have been guessing; reading them first is what made the re-queue evidence-based.

### Blast radius, restated

`new MetadataFacade` appears only in test files and one migration doc — **no production caller constructs one**. The defect was dormant and becomes live the moment a host wires the facade; the class is exported from the package root, so downstream hosts pick up the fix via the patch changeset on `@objectstack/objectql`.
